answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a meaningful onyx bond before it may transact: creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital per identity, while honest agents earn the bond back through useful work. Reputation flows like a river, accumulating slowly from verified deliveries and draining fast after fraud, so a fresh nebula of sock-puppet accounts starts with zero trust and cannot outvote established participants. The bond plus slow reputation makes mass fakery unprofitable.
